failures is only sufficient to reject independence. The converse\u2014that observed independence (zero historical correlation) implies true causal independence\u2014is a negative claim that cannot be established by observational data alone. To responsibly assert independence from a shared cause, one must audit the causal pathways that produce each node and establish that they share no common bottleneck or input. For a large centralized service, a single operator controls this audit and could theoretically provide it. For a decentralized network of independent operators, no such single operator exists, so no node can unilaterally prove that all nodes lack a shared dependence.
